root_cause.text: AppArmor’s new `__unix_needs_revalidation()` path in `security/apparmor/file.c` assumed the passed socket always had a valid `sock->sk` and unconditionally dereferenced `sock->sk->sk_family`, causing a NULL pointer dereference during SCM_RIGHTS file descriptor receive when sockets are still being set up or torn down.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!sock || !sock->sk) return false;` immediately before `if (sock->sk->sk_family == PF_UNIX)`, and the CVE text says “both the socket pointer and the socket's sk pointer can be NULL during socket setup or teardown” and that the function “dereferences sock->sk->sk_family without checking if either sock or sock->sk is NULL first.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent NULL dereference in UNIX socket revalidation by skipping checks when the socket or its sk pointer is not yet available.
intent_record.what: A new null-check block was added in __unix_needs_revalidation() before accessing sock->sk: it now returns false if either sock is NULL or sock->sk is NULL, with an added comment noting this can happen while sockets are being set up or torn down.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function avoids dereferencing an uninitialized or partially torn-down socket pointer, preventing a NULL pointer access during revalidation and causing such cases to be treated as not needing revalidation.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent NULL dereference in UNIX socket revalidation by skipping checks when the socket or its sk pointer is not yet available.
